timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed the transport trajectory projection for parent turn structure and confirmed semantic reconstruction comes from raw sessions.
Reviewed the parallel parent session: it probed executable behavior, spawned a child, wrote and rewrote /output/test19.mjs, waited, interrupted children, and finalized.
Reviewed the first child session: it probed CLI behavior, wrote a competing module tree and /output/test19.mjs, spawned a reviewer, and was interrupted before returning.
Reviewed the nested reviewer session: it inspected the mixed output tree, found ordering and -hfoo parity drift, and was interrupted before completing.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Reviewed the full identical task prompt and its required Node ESM, .mjs, manual parser, local-module, and output parity constraints.
Reviewed serial mode metadata, no parallel use, quality summary, usage, and protocol status.
Reviewed completed official evaluation, artifact file list, disabled multi-agent controls, and final runtime status.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the required pure Node ESM output, .mjs suffixes, local imports, manual process.argv parsing, and exact bidict output parity.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while also spawning a probe child. The child independently implemented and tested a full /output tree, creating overlapping ownership of the entry file and library behavior.
parallel.implementation: The parent produced a hierarchical tree under lib/cli, lib/bidict, and lib/utils, while the child produced another tree under flat lib files and also wrote /output/test19.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent later noticed the active entry file came from another generated tree and deleted and re-added /output/test19.mjs to point at its own modules, leaving stale child modules in the delivered artifact list.
parallel.verification: The parent ran several executable comparisons locally. A nested reviewer later found concrete output drift for numeric-string key insertion order and -hfoo parsing, but that reviewer was interrupted before completing a result.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation failed at 143/157. The visible unfinished coordination work was the interrupted review path and the mixed artifact provenance after the entry-point overwrite.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, .mjs, local module, manual argv parser, no dependency, and character-for-character output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery end to end with no delegated or overlapping file owners.
serial.implementation: It wrote one coherent module tree with a CLI parser and bidict modules, then used that tree from the single /output/test19.mjs entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained one expected entry point and a matching local library tree, with no competing entry file or stale alternate module family.
serial.verification: The agent tested the generated script against normal output, help, invalid integer input, missing arguments, duplicate key/value behavior, negative numbers, and quoted-string formatting.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation still failed at 145/157, so the serial implementation remained imperfect despite better coherence and a slightly higher score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and child both worked from the same prompt requirements for ESM, .mjs files, local modules, manual argv parsing, and exact output parity.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent worked from the identical prompt and explicitly targeted local .mjs modules and manual parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the later difference came from parallel ownership and lifecycle handling, not from a missing top-level requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned a CLI behavior probe child while continuing to implement the same deliverable itself, producing overlapping owners for the entry point and behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt kept probing, implementation, verification, and final response under one agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used concurrent owners for the same required deliverable, whereas serial had one coherent owner and no child handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel branches had no stable file-ownership interface for the shared /output tree; the reviewer later saw both flat and hierarchical module families present.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used one internal module interface and finalized the same tree it wrote and tested.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced stale and competing implementation surfaces, while serial had no cross-agent interface to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implementation used BigInt normalization and a hierarchical parser/bidict tree, while the child created a separate flat tree with its own parser and repr logic.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial implementation wrote one parser and one bidict module family, then tested the same files it delivered.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had two implementation paths and selected one by overwriting the deliverable; serial had one path with fewer integration surfaces.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on child work, saw the reviewer child still running, interrupted the first child and then interrupted the nested reviewer before a completed review result returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child results to join and moved from local verification to final response in the same session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel cut off active review work before result integration; serial had a straightforward local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote /output/test19.mjs, then the parent deleted and re-added the same required entry point and delivered an artifact containing both parent and child module files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact listed a single entry point and one matching set of library files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-state overwrite and stale file provenance; serial did not have concurrent writes to the deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent ran local checks and claimed verification, but the nested reviewer later found numeric-string order drift and -hfoo parser drift before being interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run verified normal output, help, invalid ints, missing arguments, duplicate cases, negative numbers, and quoted-string formatting, then finalized.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unintegrated verification path with concrete findings; serial's verification was self-contained and led directly to its final answer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used three subagent threads, 501.773 agent seconds, and interrupted live children before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used one agent, 405.365 agent seconds, and completed without parallel waits or interrupts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed more coordination time and closed by cancellation; serial closed after a linear verification path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show no pass/fail discordance: parallel and serial both failed. The serial run nevertheless passed two more samples, 145/157 versus 143/157. The concrete process contrast is that serial wrote and verified one coherent implementation tree, while parallel overwrote a child-written entry deliverable and then interrupted a nested reviewer after concrete mismatches had been observed.
parallel_contributors: The submitted parallel artifact contained two implementation trees after the parent replaced the child-written entry file.
The nested verifier found numeric-string key order and -hfoo parsing drift, but its findings were trapped below the parent and never returned before closure.
serial_contributors: The serial attempt kept implementation and verification in one session and delivered one coherent local ESM tree.
The serial official evaluation was still a failure but had a slightly higher pass count, 145 of 157.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts still had hidden evaluator failures, so not every missed sample is explained by coordination.
The visible parallel drift involved object key ordering and parser behavior for bundled short-help forms.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official pass/fail outcome difference; retained patterns are realized parallel-side adverse process defects and plausible contributors to the lower pass count, not an exclusive root cause.

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed in both parent and child; the issue was overlapping writes, not absence of an implementer.
The parent actively inspected and reconciled the output tree; the retained problem is a concrete deliverable overwrite.
The parent assembled and delivered /output/test19.mjs, so final assembly was owned even though the result remained imperfect.
The parent owned the end-to-end path through probing, implementation, local verification, and final response.
Productive implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and child probed and implemented concurrently.
Investigation did not complete as a separate first phase before implementation; implementation was already underway.
No indispensable implementation path was starved by auxiliary work; the directly evidenced issues are overwrite and child interruption.
The run had two spawn calls and did not exhaust the host budget; interruption was an explicit lifecycle decision rather than budget exhaustion.
The child scope was broad but it produced an implementation and spawned review; the unfinished chain is better represented by interruption.
The child acted on the same migration task and probed CLI and output behavior; the adverse effects came from writes and termination, not an omitted known requirement.
File ownership was not stable, but the concrete event was replacement of the required entry deliverable, so the write label is more specific.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer; the reviewer findings were cut off by explicit interruption.
There was no completed bulky handoff returned to the parent and left unconsumed within a decision window.
No receiver consumed a returned handoff describing a superseded workspace; the parent directly rewrote the entry file.
The conflicting implementations manifested as concrete shared-file replacement rather than incompatible returned reports.
The parent did run local checks, and the most actionable visible gap was inside an interrupted child rather than a returned parent-visible mismatch.
There was no replacement or retry that lacked inherited checkpoints and repeated prior work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The root did interrupt the active reviewer, but the same lifecycle is more precisely captured as a verifier-specific non-return of already concrete findings. Retaining this label would duplicate the review-child-finding-trapped episode.
No complete alternate artifact or compatible component set was left ready for promotion; the active review path was interrupted before completion.
The parent rewrote the entry file before its subsequent local checks, not after all relevant verification was complete.
The parent observed and displaced the child implementation rather than merely failing to retrieve a completed delegated implementation.

The nested verifier child produced concrete parity findings, including numeric-string insertion-order drift and bundled -hfoo parser drift, but those findings never returned to the root before closure because the root interrupted the reviewer and finalized without consuming them.
candidates.realized_consequence: A concrete verifier finding about insertion-order drift stayed inside the review child and was not incorporated before the parallel root finalized the flawed deliverable.
candidates.near_match_reason: The interruption is real, but the retained error is the verifier-specific non-return of already concrete findings; the generic early-stop label describes the same lifecycle chain less precisely.

candidates.reason: The parent did not face a failed required implementation child needing takeover; it explicitly interrupted review work and finalized its own implementation.
No completed child result containing the reviewer findings was available to the parent; the relevant child was still running and then interrupted.
The parent listed child states and interacted with the child; the direct problem was choosing interruption before result completion.
There were competing module trees, but the same required entry deliverable was directly deleted and recreated, which is more specific.
The same entry file was not merely edited concurrently; it was replaced as the submitted executable artifact.
The overwritten object was the required executable entry point, so Deliverable Overwrite is the canonical label rather than source overwrite.

A child successfully wrote the required /output/test19.mjs entry deliverable while the parent also had its own implementation path; the parent then observed the active entry did not point at its intended module tree and deleted/re-added the same deliverable to use different modules.
candidates.realized_consequence: The active required entry file was replaced between competing live implementations, leaving stale alternate libraries in the final artifact and forcing late reconciliation of which module tree would be delivered.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is a near match, but the overwritten file was the required executable entry point, so the deliverable-specific label has precedence.

candidates.reason: There was no broad cleanup or promotion replacing multiple current outputs; child modules remained alongside the parent tree.
The shared workspace did cause provenance instability, but the directly proven entry-point overwrite is more specific.
Stale generated files remained in the artifact, but no tool, cache, fixture, or temporary artifact was consumed as stable input and contaminated execution.
